title: Image Prompt Library — content.json contract
description: Input contract for the QUERY operation (SPEC section 7). product.attributes exists so every skeleton conditional resolves from structured data instead of LLM inference — the fields mirror the conditionals that exist in the registry (G7-X mode of use, G8 visible output, pose/light branches, real colorways).

reference_photos.description: Content hashes of product reference photos (files live outside the repo, SPEC 6.4). MAY BE EMPTY, and an empty array is a statement rather than a gap: the export carried no product photograph, so there is nothing to hash and nothing is invented. The prompts still carry their G1 reference block and stay paste-and-run — the owner attaches the photo by hand in the generation tool (ADR-021, query/runbook.md Step 5). minItems was 1 until ADR-035, which is why six of eight routed sessions failed the contract SPEC 1 says they satisfy.

operation.description: active = user operates it mid-action (pose branch); passive = it works while the user does something else.

visible_output.description: What the product visibly emits: mist | spray | water-jet | steam | foam | light | particles | none. Drives G8 (visible mechanism) and the LIGHT branch. Use 'none' when nothing is visible — never invent an effect.

mounting.description: The single mode of use every layer must share (G7-X).

colorways.description: REAL colorways only — fabricated colorways are a G2 violation.

body_contact.description: Whether the product acts on a body structure (gates 03-mechanism-ghostbody).

symptom_visibility.description: Can the problem's symptoms be photographed? Gates 01-pain-split and the symptom-rail vignette mode.

result_visibility.description: Where the result can be seen. 'invisible' kills 06-relief-scene (verified boundary).

specification.description: The manufacturer's own component and capability line, verbatim. Step 5 fills component names from this and from raw_features and from nowhere else: 03-mechanism-xray and 03-mechanism-ghostbody both admit only component types the product genuinely contains, so a prompt that names a pump, a bladder or a backlight panel needs a source that says so. Without it content.json cannot reproduce its own prompts, which SPEC 1 claims it can.

raw_features.description: Feature claims as the brief states them, one per entry. Distinct from problems_solved, which is what the buyer suffers, and from specification, which is what the manufacturer certifies. Optional: a page whose images argue no mechanism needs neither.

lpTypeId.description: PROVENANCE ONLY — the flunnel page-export's own template id (`pdp_dr`, `listicle`, ...), recorded so a content.json can say which export and which block map produced it. NOTHING READS IT TO ROUTE. ADR-059 removed channel as an admission test precisely because the router had been guessing the channel from this value for five sessions running; recording a fact is not the same as gating on it, and this is the treatment `channels` already has in type frontmatter — kept as a record of where something came from, read by nothing that admits or refuses. The converter DOES read it, upstream of this file, to choose which block map applies: two exports measured 2026-09-11 share no argued block key at all. Optional (ADR-081), so every content.json written before it stays valid, and a hand-written one has no export to name.
